content.text:
**Finding: deviation (EXCLUSIVITY, high severity)**

Section 6.1 ("Exclusivity") binds us, the Company: for the entire term we cannot participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products *or* substantially similar products (expressly including competitors' lines), while HDI holds the exclusive online rights to the "Deerskin" brand.

Why it fails the fallback:
- **Duration is effectively open-ended** — Section 4.1 gives a one-year term that auto-renews on every anniversary, so exclusivity rolls indefinitely rather than being capped at 12 months.
- **No performance-based exit** — apart from the one-time launch right in Section 1.6 (70 days to go live), exclusivity survives HDI failing to keep the Site operational; and our 90-day exit triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a), so exiting is penalised.
- **Category is broader than needed** — it reaches products merely "substantially similar" to Deerskin Products.

Redline (validated, fallback level): exclusivity narrowed to Deerskin Products, capped at 12 months from the Effective Date, and terminating automatically on HDI's launch failure or an uncured material performance failure under Sections 1 or 5. We deliberately left HDI's reciprocal two-year non-compete in Section 6.3 and HDI's brand exclusivity intact, since those parts of the bargain work in our favour — which is also why we went to the fallback rather than striking the clause outright.
